title: This One Line Crashes Your URL Shortener

sourceReview.learningGoal: Explain how a synchronous click counter creates row contention and how batching removes per-click database writes.
sourceReview.caveat: Rates and latency are illustrative. Redis INCR still adds a network call; GETDEL plus SQL is not crash-safe or exactly-once. Counts can lag or be lost without durable processing.

claims.claim: In PostgreSQL (and InnoDB), concurrent UPDATEs to the same row are serialized by a row-level lock: each transaction waits for the previous one holding the lock to commit or roll back.

Under high concurrency on one hot row, this queuing raises per-request latency sharply and holds database connections while waiting, which can exhaust the connection pool and slow unrelated queries/links.
The redirect path of a URL shortener is the hot, read-heavy path; adding a synchronous DB write per redirect turns every click into a write.

Standard fix: record clicks off the critical path — increment an in-memory counter (e.g. Redis INCR, which is atomic) or enqueue a click event (Kafka/queue), return the redirect immediately, and have a background worker aggregate and flush counts to the DB periodically (one write per interval instead of one per click).

Trade-off: counts shown to the owner lag by the flush interval (seconds); a crash between INCR and flush can lose or delay a small window of counts unless the counter store is durable — acceptable for analytics, not for money.
'20ms → 4,800ms' and '10,000 clicks/sec' are illustrative numbers for the scenario, not measured benchmarks; presented on screen as an example, not a claim about a specific system.

beats.headline:
STOP COUNTING
CLICKS LIKE THIS
beats.narration: Ek influencer ne tumhara short link share kiya. Das hazaar clicks per second. Aur tumhara poora URL shortener — sirf ek line ki wajah se band ho gaya.

beats.headline:
The demo passes.
Production waits.
beats.subhead: A synchronous UPDATE inside every redirect.
beats.narration: Interviewer bolta hai: owner ko click count dikhana hai. Tum redirect mein clicks plus one daal dete ho. Ek request pe test pass, demo perfect.

beats.headline:
A read path.
A write on every click.
beats.subhead: Your cache saved a read. Your counter added a write.
beats.narration: Destination Redis se laaye the taaki database ko chhuna na pade. Lekin counter? Har click pe database write. Redirect ka sabse garam rasta ab write ka wait kar raha hai.

beats.headline:
One row. One lock.
Everyone waits.
beats.subhead: Concurrent updates serialize on the hot row.
beats.narration: Das hazaar clicks, sab ek hi row update karna chahte hain. Ek transaction row lock pakadta hai, baaki line mein. Twenty milliseconds wala redirect ab seconds leta hai.

metric.label: Contention
metric.value: One row lock at a time

beats.headline:
One counter.
The whole product down.
beats.subhead: Waiting writes hold shared database connections.
beats.narration: Connections usi line mein phanse hain. Ab doosre links ko bhi connection nahi milta. Sale aur docs jaise links timeout. Ek hot counter, poora product slow.

beats.headline:
Keep SQL writes
off the hot path.
beats.subhead: Increment in memory, then return the redirect.
beats.narration: Fix: click Redis counter mein daalo aur user ko turant destination bhejo. Redirect ko har click par database UPDATE ka wait mat karao.

beats.headline:
Many clicks.
One batched write.
beats.subhead: A background worker aggregates every five seconds.
beats.narration: Background worker har paanch second clicks jod ke database mein ek baar likhta hai. Ek batch mein das hazaar events ho, toh das hazaar writes ki jagah ek.

beats.headline:
Counts can lag.
Redirects cannot.
beats.subhead: State the trade-off before the interviewer asks.
beats.narration: Tradeoff khud bolo: count paanch second late dikhega. Analytics late chal sakta hai, redirect slow nahi. Crash pe counts bachane ke liye durability alag design karni hogi.

beats.headline:
Two users.
One /launch.
beats.narration: Kal: do log ek saath slash launch maangte hain. System dono ko bolta hai: ye tumhara hai. Kya tootega?
